title: From Table-Toppers to Desperate: Inside Punjab Kings' Stunning Five-Match Collapse
excerpt: PBKS went from 6-1 to 6-6 in a fortnight, and now face must-win matches against RCB and LSG to keep playoff hopes alive
body:
There is a particular cruelty in the IPL's unforgiving format: the same relentless schedule that allows a team to surge up the table can destroy them just as quickly. Punjab Kings are learning this the hard way.

After winning six of their first seven matches — including the season's solitary no-result — PBKS sat atop the IPL 2026 standings, their best start in franchise history. Captain Shreyas Iyer was being discussed as a potential Orange Cap contender. Head coach Ricky Ponting was drawing praise for transforming a perennial underachiever into a genuine title threat. The Punjabi heartland, and its vast diaspora, dared to believe.

Then came the collapse. Five consecutive defeats have dropped PBKS from first to fourth, their net run rate cratering and their playoff qualification — which once seemed certain — now dependent on results elsewhere.

## What went wrong

The post-mortem is uncomfortable reading. Against Mumbai Indians on May 14, PBKS posted 200-plus — ordinarily a winning total — only to watch Tilak Varma dismantle their bowling with a composed 75. It was a microcosm of the losing streak: competitive with the bat, catastrophic with the ball.

"It's a tough pill to swallow," Iyer admitted after the MI defeat, his frustration barely concealed. The captain's own form has been solid, but his inability to influence results from the middle order has exposed a deeper structural problem.

Assistant coach Brad Haddin, filling in at press conferences with the blunt pragmatism of an Australian, urged the squad to stay off social media. "There are going to be ups and downs," he said after a fourth consecutive loss to Delhi Capitals. "The guys need to block out the noise and focus on what they can control."

## The bowling crisis

Punjab's collapse is fundamentally a bowling problem. During the six-win surge, the PBKS attack operated with discipline and death-overs nous that exceeded expectations. That discipline has evaporated. Opponents have chased down targets with increasing ease, exploiting predictable lengths and an over-reliance on pace at the death.

The Arshdeep Singh controversy — in which the left-arm quick faced racism allegations on social media after a heated exchange with Tilak Varma during the MI match — has added unwanted noise to an already fragile dressing room. While the incident itself was a social media storm rather than a cricketing crisis, it symbolised the pressure cooker that PBKS have become.

## The road to qualification

The mathematics remains in PBKS's favour, but only just. At 13 points from 12 matches, they sit fourth — the last playoff spot. But Rajasthan Royals (12 points, 11 played) and Chennai Super Kings (12 points) are breathing down their necks, while Kolkata Knight Riders, freshly buoyed by a 29-run demolition of Gujarat Titans, have surged to 11 points and could leapfrog with a couple of wins.

Today's match against Royal Challengers Bengaluru at the PCA Stadium in Mohali is, by any measure, the biggest game in PBKS's season. RCB, sitting pretty at the top with 16 points, have the luxury of experimentation. Punjab have no such margin. A loss would leave their fate entirely in others' hands.

## The Punjabi diaspora's emotional investment

No IPL franchise carries the emotional weight of its regional identity quite like Punjab Kings. The team's fanbase extends deep into the Punjabi diaspora — the largest and most visible Indian community in Canada, a significant presence in the UK's Midlands and London, and a growing force in California and New York.

For these fans, PBKS is not just a cricket franchise. It is a cultural marker, a thread connecting second-generation Canadians in Brampton to the PCA Stadium in Mohali. The five-match collapse has been discussed in Punjabi-language WhatsApp groups, gurdwara conversations, and diaspora sports podcasts with an intensity that reflects how personal this team's fortunes feel.

## What needs to change

Ponting's challenge is immediate and tactical: fix the death bowling, restore Arshdeep's confidence, and convince a squad that was riding high three weeks ago that the sky is not falling. The broader challenge is psychological. Teams that collapse in the IPL rarely recover within the same season — the format's pace leaves little time for reflection or reinvention.

PBKS have two matches left to save their season. Whether they can summon the form that made them table-toppers, rather than the fragility that made them free-fall, will determine whether this season is remembered as a breakthrough or the most painful near-miss in franchise history.
